title: Homogenization of Anisotropic <mark>Lithium</mark> Diffusion in Polycrystalline Battery Electrode Particles
authors: Robert M. Hoffman, Kasra Taghikhani, William J. Parnell, J. R. Berger and Robert J. Kee
abstract: The diffusion coefficient is a fundamental parameter for modeling the performance of different types of batteries. Standard battery models typically assume an isotropic and constant diffusion coefficient. However, most commonly used battery electrodes contain smaller primary particles with layered crystalline lattice structures, with fast in-plane and slow cross-plane transport. Isotropic assumptions thus fail to capture the inherent structural anisotropy of the polycrystalline secondary particles structures that make up the battery electrode. The current study investigates the effect of grain…

title: Interplay Between the GDL Mechanical Properties and the Flow Field Structure in PEMFCs
authors: Marcus Ringström, Henrik Ekström, Göran Lindbergh and Rakel Wreland Lindström
abstract: The performance of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) is strongly influenced by the mechanical deformation of the gas diffusion layer (GDL) under assembly compression. Despite the orthotropic mechanical behavior of GDLs, the coupled effects of directional stiffness and flow-field geometry on PEMFC performance remain insufficiently understood. In this work, a coupled mechanical–electrochemical computational framework is developed to quantify the influence of GDL orthotropic mechanical properties across different channel-to-rib ratios. title: Sulfurization-Time-Regulated Structural Evolution and Alkaline HER/OER Performance of Self-Supported Ni Sulfide/CeO2 Electrodes
authors: Zhijing Yu, Yi Gan, Yuting Zhou, Zidan Yang, Yang Song and Liwen Hu
abstract: Sulfurization duration is a critical yet frequently empirical parameter in the fabrication of nickel <mark>sulfide-based</mark> self-supported electrodes. Herein, Ni sulfide/CeO2 electrodes were prepared on nickel foam by electrodeposition followed by thermal sulfurization at 350 °C for 1 ∼ 4 h to investigate the effects of sulfurization duration on their phase composition, morphology, surface chemical states, and alkaline HER/OER performance.
